recipes.name: Prime Rib Soup
ingredients_raw: 4 beef ribs, trimmed from a cooked prime rib roast
1 potato, peeled and cut into 3/4 inch pieces

steps.text: Place ribs in a large pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the meat is falling from the bones, about 2 hours.
Remove ribs and allow to cool. Trim the meat from the ribs and cut into bite-sized pieces; refrigerate.
Continue simmering broth until reduced to 1 cup; refrigerate until the fat congeals to the top.

Pour broth into a saucepan along with meat trimmings, beef stock, potato, carrots, mushrooms, salt, and pepper. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until potatoes are tender, about 20 minutes. Sprinkle with chives to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Prime Rib Soup
raw_recipe.description: This delicious prime rib soup uses leftover bones from a prime rib roast to easily make into a tasty recipe. Everyone loves this comforting meal.

review.reviewBody: This soup was excellent and an superb way to use up our Christmas Eve prime rib. My family of 7 loved it and I loved the idea of not wasting a single ounce of an expensive prime rib (including the bones). Made as directed, but next year I will try simmering the bones in my crockpot overnight and then the next day doing the reduction. This might save on time because like another reviewer stated this took longer time period to reduce than the recipe called for. Since there were no measurements on the amount of water to cover on the bones, this time would vary person to person, depending on how much water they used. I simmered for about 2.5 hours on the stove and then finally ended up just boiling to reduce. Hence my idea to use my crockpot next time then either do a boiled reduction or do a simmering reduction. Thanks Emily! It was a hit with all 5 of my kids, and it was a hit with me because I finally have an awesome recipe to us with prime rib leftovers.

Loved this recipe. I had a 12 pound prime rib so I had 5 bones. I upped the recipe accordingly. I also knew I would want more meat so I cleaned and cubed a steak sized portion to add to the ribs so we could have more meat in the dish. So I guess I made it a stew/soup. Yes it is time consuming, but what good soup or stew isn't. Because I heavily season my prime rib roasts, I waited until after I added all the cooked ingredients before adding any salt or pepper. I did not add mushrooms because even though I love everything else, that is one thing this cook doesn't eat! lol I also chopped about three quarters of a bunch of green onions and threw them in about 5 min before it were finished to get some of the flavor into the soup. Bottom line is... the flavors were great, it was worth the effort and I look forward to making it again after my next prime rib. Thank you Emily!

This recipe needed adjustments. Added red wine and Kitchen Bouquet to make broth richer. Also used Portabello Mushrooms, not button, and added onions, carrots & garlic to give it more depth. Definitely time consuming but well worth it. Served with crusty Artisan Bread and we couldn't get enough.

VERY good soup! I did start with sauteing chopped onion and celery in butter, then added the prime rib, beef stock; added carrots and two potatoes. I already had rosemary, garlic & thyme coated on my prime rib from the day before, so that added wonderful flavor. Thanks Emily! This was so good and a great way to use up every bit of that expensive Christmas prime rib! KEEPER!
Excellent recipe. I added a few things as I always do. Worcestershire sauce, flour, half and half,carrots, garlic ,onion rosemary and thyme. Thickened it up a bit.

Made this in my Ninja Crock Pot. Used our leftover Prime Rib and bones from Christmas eve and let it cook done ALL day. Sauteed some shallots and fresh garlic then added 2 32 oz cartons of Beef stock. About an hour before I served it I added carrots, potatoes and mushrooms. Added a dash of Worcestershire sauce, fresh rosemary and black pepper. No need for other seasonings as the Prime Rib was already pre-seasoned when I bought it. I did add flour to thicken it up. AMAZING flavor! Definitely want to make this again.

I used a 7 rib 18 pounder for New Years. It was easy to cook and came out great. I cooked down all the ribs in a crock pot overnight. Pull the bone from the meat and let the meat cool too. Its easier to seperate the fats and connective tissues when cold. I also doubled the broth and added some chicken bouillion (shhh..dont tell the ribs), also a few each celery and carrots. Turned out great and made myself feel good about spending so much on the initial roast. Enjoy
This was great! I added some more veggies, used two cans of beef broth and a some steak seasoning. A great use of left-over prime rib when you just can't eat another sandwich.

This is a wonderful recipe for leftover prime rib bones. I, like many others, I added some extras like carrots, onions, and garlic which I sautéed in olive oil with mushrooms before adding the other ingredients. After we had eaten our prime rib the day before, I drained off the fat in the bottom of the pan and put some hot water in to the drippings so I could save them. I had 2 cups of very seasoned and rich broth from that. The next day I put the bones and one leftover slice of meat in the crockpot and covered it with water. It actually cooked all night long and part of the next day, about 15 hours. I removed the meat and bones and strained all of the broth. I put it in a large measuring cup and set that in a pan with an ice bath. Within an hour the fat had congealed on the top and easy to remove. So there really was no fat in the soup to speak of. I also added a splash of red wine just to add to the complexity of flavors. In the last few minutes I added about 3/4 c gluten free tagliatelle noodles and then about one tablespoon cornstarch mixed with a little water, just to give it a velvety look and taste. Oh boy, is this ever a delicious way to use a prime rib bone or two. I had two. Thank you for the recipe. It is probably delicious, and quicker, just as written.

4-2-2018 ~After all my years of cooking and baking, it still is remarkable to me what one can put on the dinner table that is nourishing, delicious, and inexpensive all at once. A soup like this is a case in point. Think about it – a couple of bones (prime rib or otherwise), simmered for hours, with everything but the kitchen sink (whatever you have on hand basically) added to the broth to make a substantial soup. I’ve been making soup like this for decades, and I followed this recipe loosely. I find no need to reduce the broth. If you’ve got “good bones,” pun intended, and enough of them, there is no need for that. I did use roasted prime rib bones, some meat attached, along with celery and its leaves, parsley, a few cloves of garlic, a little salt, a bit of tomato paste and a glug of red wine. Something I tried that was new for me was to make this in the slow cooker and while it turned out perfectly, I really didn’t find any particular advantage to that. Not a fan of potatoes in soup, after straining the broth I used an appropriate pasta for soup instead, along with some odds and ends I had in the fridge – mushrooms, carrots, zucchini and celery. This was a home run tonight, as it always is.
A little time consuming, but it's worth it! I used barley instead of the potato, just because that's what I had handy. Came out excellent!

Used a 4 bone rack and cooked it in beef broth with carrots, celery, onion, garlic, Parmesan rind and 2 bay leaves all in a soup sack. Boiled gently for 4+ hrs until meat on bones was extremely tender and the rack of bones fell apart. Took the bones, meat and bag of seasonings out of broth. I kept the meat and the carrots, the rest i discarded. Let chill overnight, then skimmed off fat cap. The next day I added potato, mushroom, carrots and the prime rib meat into broth. Served with Parmesan Cheese. Delicious
Followed this recipe last year and doing again today. In the slow cooker for the whole day. I do add carrots, and pearl onions, and lil potatoes. Yum, my favorite beef soup.
Great soup! It takes a little while to boil the broth with the bones in it, but it has fabulous flavor. I would definitely make it again.

This recipe caught my eye because the photos display carrots but the recipe doesn’t include them. I modified it considerably. 1. No additional salt needed if adding commercially available beef broth. 2. Chives are not detectable in rich beef. Add pearl or green onions instead. 3. Added a cup of frozen mixed veggies & 1/2 cup barley. So yummy
Great recipe! I used Beef Bone Broth and added carrots and pearl onions. OMG!

A great way to use the bones from Prime Rib being I have no dog. I did not need to use the beef broth, I used all the broth (8cups water) from simmering the bones for about 3hrs....skimmed the fat and cooked down the broth to about 6 cups of liquid. Sautéed 2 med. onions and 2 celery stakes in a Tbls of butter before adding to broth. I tripled the mushrooms because we love mushrooms and doubled up on the potatoes. Added tsp thyme and a Tbls of Worcestershire sauce and last but not least a package of brown gravy mix....my husband loved it and so did I....will certainly make this again...thanks for the starting point to a great soup...next time I'll save a little more meat to put in!

Thanks so much for in the inspiration. I made it with green onions in the soup, chopped celery, cubed potatoes and the mushrooms- no added salt or pepper as my butcher seasons the entire prime rib, and then cuts the bones free but ties them back up for roasting. Stopped reducing at about 2 1/2 cups -ended with about 1 1/4 after removing the fat - added a 32 ounce package of beef stock - and it is absolutely delicious.
